text:
jamie: flagging a design gap we hit on the Private onboarding checklist: we need a clear minimal protocol for a runtime to declare what secret workflows it supports so control plane and console UX can behave safely. thoughts?

luis: +1. We've been juggling 3 patterns in docs: full push (control plane supplies creds), reference+pull (runtime fetches from customer KMS), and blinded bootstrap (encrypted one-shot token). No single runtime supports all three today.

rachel: proposal: define a 2-part surface: (1) capability declaration endpoint on runtime, (2) a non-sensitive auth probe endpoint. Keep both tiny.

theo: sounds sane. Example capability keys: `pull_kms`, `hsm_bound`, `accept_bootstrap_token`, `local_secret_cache_ttl_ms`. Keep values boolean/int.

jamie: agree. How should control plane act on missing capability responses? degrade to push model? warn?

luis: fallback plan: if runtime is old (no /capabilities) assume push-only and mark runtime as "legacy-secret-mode" in UI. But we should treat that deprecated and set migration timeline in RFC.

marta: ops note: pushing plaintext creds is a big compliance flag for Private customers. Any push path must be opt-in and audited. Prefer reference-first by default.

rachel: UX flow for reference-first: when user supplies a manifest with `secrets: model_key: "kms://..."` the control plane shows a preflight state where it calls `/probe-auth`. Probe should not return secrets — just status codes and small reasons (KMS_UNREACHABLE, NO_PERMISSION, OK).

theo: implement probe as `POST /probe-auth` with body listing the set of references it will try. Response 200 + {ok:true, failures:[]}, or 502 with `reason:KMS_UNREACHABLE`. Keep payload tiny so logs safe.

jamie: any encryption binding ideas for bootstrap token? we should avoid plaintext token in transit if possible.

luis: encrypt bootstrap token to the runtime's attested public key (TPM/HSM). Control plane stores ciphertext only temporarily. On issuance, emit audit event `bootstrap_token_issued` with customer id and runtime id, no token value.
\rm: (typo)

ops-bot: alert 1789995000: recent customer reported stuck spin-ups due to KMS egress blocked by firewall rules. linking.

rachel: for that scenario, bootstrap token is useful: control plane issues encrypted bootstrap, runtime decrypts locally, uses token to fetch secrets, then erases it. TTL should be small, default 300s, configurable per-account.

theo: note: KMS pull adds latency on cold start. recommend local secret cache with configurable TTL and a key rotation hook. Document cold-start penalty in RFC (50-350ms depending on region).

jamie: telemetry: we need 3 labels: secret_flow=(reference|push|bootstrap), probe_status=(OK|UNREACHABLE|DENIED), bootstrap_issued=(true|false). Must ensure no secret material in logs.

luis: and a runtime capability version field so we can gate console behavior by `capabilities_version` to allow future extension.

marta: rollout plan suggestion: P0: capability + probe endpoints in runtime 1.2. P1: console UX switch to default-to-reference for accounts with `capabilities.pull_kms=true`. P2: deprecate push-only runtimes after 3 months.

jamie: action items: 1) theo to draft API contract for `/capabilities` and `/probe-auth` (mini-PR) due Tue. 2) rachel to sketch UX flows and audit events. 3) luis to draft bootstrap encryption pattern and sample manifest snippet. 4) eng-sre to add telemetry labels and a dashboard for probe failures.

luis: sample manifest snippet i'll include: ```
secrets:
  model_key_ref: "kms://proj/acme/key/model-serve"
  secret_policy:
    bootstrap_enabled: true
    bootstrap_ttl_seconds: 300
```

rachel: one more operational rule: control plane must refuse to push long-lived secrets to runtimes that advertise `accept_bootstrap_token=false` unless customer explicitly enables legacy push. Add that to docs.

marta: good. If no objections i'll consolidate into a short RFC and post for review. prefer we avoid introducing a new long-lived secret transfer pattern.

jamie: no objections. thanks everyone — i'll file RFC with the contract sketch and an onboarding checklist entry.
